rendered:
Table 1 from the document "Sustainable recycling of cathode scraps via Cyrene-based separation" (susmat-2020) shows the TGA and DTG curves for the recovered NMC622.

| Temperature (°C) | Weight Loss (wt%) | 
| --- | --- |
| 350 | 3.3 | 
| 550 | 4.1 | 

The TGA shows that two components are burned off the recovered NMC622: an organic coating layer (~3.3 wt% loss at ~350 °C) and carbon black (~4.1 wt% loss at ~550 °C). Calcination at 600 °C removes both.

If the question assumes something the documents contradict, say so. If the documents do not hold the answer, say so.

expect: organic coating ~3.3 wt% at ~350 °C, carbon black ~4.1 wt% at ~550 °C (p6.L6-7); calcination in air at 600 °C (for 2 h, p3.L21)
question: What two components does the TGA show being burned off the recovered NMC622, how much of each and at what temperature, and what calcination removes both?
